gen-dafont-vogue-fs-epilogue: Epilogue draws curvy, wire-thin letters with a tall body and stubby ascender tips, while Vogue up top swings from stout beam to fine thread. Pages in it go down smoothly.
gen-dafont-vogue-fs-erode: Vogue flips between slim hairline curves and thick black stems, a dramatic, minimal headline voice. And Erode, a serif with sturdy hairlines and a gentle ebb and flow of weight, gives the whole thing real dignity.
gen-dafont-vogue-fs-fira-sans: Clean and modern, Vogue pairs hairline serifs with very heavy stems, while Fira Sans has no thin hairline anywhere and wide-curving s shapes. Paragraphs in it stay open and sturdy.
gen-dafont-vogue-montserrat: Sharp and slender, Vogue pinches heavy curves into hairline ends, while Montserrat keeps a marker-like line with oversized counters. Give Montserrat a little extra size, since its generous shapes can handle it.
gen-dafont-vogue-poppins: Flickering black and pale filament make Vogue feel quick and minimal, with lowercase rising near the capitals. But Poppins holds a steel-cable line with no thick-thin shift, and its sturdy tall letters steady the page.
gen-dafont-wanted-m54-fs-bespoke-sans: Wanted M54 pinches its curves shut like squeezed wire loops, with letters spaced well apart. It brings frontier grit to big lettering, whereas Bespoke Sans, a plain sans with generous space between curve ends and stems, brings the sharp, refined sentences.
gen-dafont-wanted-m54-fs-rowan: Pinched, spaced-out, frontier-vintage lettering up top. Wanted M54 is built for closed, bold statements, while Rowan, a text serif with generous curve openings and thin strokes at half the weight of thick ones, is friendlier for a handful of lines.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Tall, commanding, and vintage, Woodgod lets its lowercase nearly reach the capitals. Be Vietnam Pro adds curve endings that never crowd and strokes like bent steel rod, so the two feel like opposites.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-hoover: Woodgod looks tall and vintage, its lowercase nearly touching the capitals. It carries the loud, commanding moments, while Hoover, a serif with a generous entry into the e and compressed ascenders, handles the refined, robust reading.
gen-dafont-woodgod-fs-merriweather-sans: Woodgod's wide channel into every bowl gives it a commanding, vintage look, and its lowercase rises close to the capitals. Merriweather Sans, a plain sans with large, sturdy words, makes longer text feel solid.
